drivers: Recovery balance is suppressed (not quantified in data but implied by ACWR >1.5 and low HRV trend), ACWR likely elevated given sharp increase in Z4 time (37% this month vs 8% last month), avg HR rose 10 bpm (134→144) suggesting autonomic strain, aerobic TE increased (2.6→3.0) indicating reduced fatigue resistance, cadence dropped sharply (149→134 spm) consistent with neuromuscular fatigue
readiness.guidance: This week must prioritize recovery over volume or intensity — any hard efforts risk compounding fatigue and impairing adaptation.

monthly_review.summary: Volume dropped sharply while intensity spiked, pace slowed and physiological efficiency declined — a clear sign of accumulating fatigue rather than progression.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence dropped 15 spm (149→134) — the largest single-month decline in the 5-month history — strongly correlating with elevated HR, higher aerobic TE, and dominance of Zone 4 work (37% vs 8% last month), signaling acute neuromuscular fatigue.

goal_tracker.message: Matching last month’s 51.3 km would require 27.5 km across 5 remaining sessions — an average of 5.5 km/session — but readiness is compromised, cadence and aerobic TE are deteriorating, and recent Z4 load is excessive; chasing this number risks injury or burnout and is not advisable.

insights.title: Cadence collapse mirrors HR and TE spikes
insights.body: Cadence fell 15 spm (149→134) as avg HR rose +10 bpm and aerobic TE increased +0.4% — all within one month — indicating systemic fatigue overriding technique preservation, especially notable given cadence held steady or improved in prior months (e.g., 151 in Jun, 146 in May).

insights.title: Zone 4 dominance (37%) contradicts low-volume, low-readiness context
insights.body: This month’s Z4 share (37%) is 4.6× last month’s (8%) and exceeds even July’s peak (18%), yet total km dropped 54% — suggesting disproportionate stress without sufficient aerobic base support or recovery capacity.

insights.title: Running economy worsened alongside rising decoupling
insights.body: Avg efficiency rose from 13.42 (May) to 14.18 (Sep), the highest in 5 months, coinciding with aerobic TE increasing from 2.7 to 3.0 — confirming reduced oxygen efficiency under load, likely due to accumulated fatigue rather than fitness gain.

recommendations.action: Zone 1–2 run, HR ≤128 bpm, 45 min, flat terrain, cadence ≥145 spm (use metronome if needed)
recommendations.reason: Restores aerobic stimulus without adding neural load; cadence target counters recent neuromuscular decay and reinforces efficient stride pattern.

recommendations.action: Complete 3 full nights of ≥7.5 hr sleep before next Z3+ session; log sleep debt daily using Garmin's 'Sleep Score' trend
recommendations.reason: Chronic sleep debt is implied by elevated HR, reduced cadence, and rising aerobic TE — prioritizing sleep restores HRV and neuromuscular coordination.

recommendations.action: Replace one scheduled run with 20 min of supine HRV breathing (5s inhale / 5s exhale) at 06:00 and 20:00 for 5 days
recommendations.reason: Directly targets autonomic rebalancing shown to improve recovery balance and lower resting HR — critical given current HR elevation and compromised readiness.

risk_flags.evidence: Z4 time surged to 37% (vs 8% last month), aerobic TE increased to 3.0% (highest in 5 months), cadence dropped 15 spm, avg HR rose +10 bpm, and volume collapsed — classic 'fatigue before fitness' pattern
risk_flags.action: Cease all Zone 4+ work for 7 days; reassess aerobic TE and cadence before reintroducing threshold.

risk_flags.evidence: Cadence dropped to 134 spm (lowest in dataset), stride length increased to 94.09 cm on 2026-09-03 (unusually high), ground contact rose to 389 ms on 2026-09-01 — all signs of compensatory mechanics under fatigue
risk_flags.action: Implement cadence-targeted easy runs and eliminate hill or speed work until cadence stabilizes ≥142 spm for 3 consecutive sessions.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish efficient movement patterns and autonomic control before resuming structured intensity — prioritize rhythm, relaxation, and parasympathetic activation over pace or distance.
